the 800 MiB of copies are host memory, not guest RSS: this host's harness work directory is under /tmp (tmpfs), so their pages are charged to Shmem — which went 4974 -> 5779 MiB (4 MiB off the copies' 800 MiB) while the fleet ran. Host-wide Cached (44039 -> 44869 MiB) moved for the whole host's reasons and is not attributed to the fleet. noded's RSS is what the 8 GiB criterion measures and does not carry the copies, so a fleet's true host cost is that RSS plus them — recorded here so it is not understated

steady-state CPU with the volume attached is 2.500% of one core versus 2.4999586269339846% without it in this run: the guest's ext4 journal adds no measurable steady-state cost here (the case without a workspace carries the 0.03%-baseline finding)

findings.title: steady-state CPU does not reproduce the recorded 0.03% baseline
findings.detail: measured peak 2.500% of one core for 50 guests with the fleet's own beats configuration versus the 0.03% recorded in PORT_STATUS slice 16. The configured bar (5.0%) still passes, with a thin margin. At n=2 the same configuration measures 0.250%. The recorded figure was sampled with the guests 'parked in HLT', which measures no heartbeat writes and no console polling; noded never boots a parked guest (its cmdline builder has no halt option), and every guest it does boot writes a heartbeat every 5 s and polls its console every second, plus the run watcher's 5 ms poll pass. Those wakeups are the measured cost. A like-for-like baseline is needed: either re-sample the recorded figure with the same guest configuration, or expose a parked-guest option through noded so both states can be measured.

findings.title: a restarted daemon reuses run-r1 and overwrites the previous instance's workspace copy
findings.detail: noded's run ids restart with the daemon (`Registry::new` sets `next_seq = 0`), so the first run after a restart is `r1` again and its workspace directory is /tmp/apz-acceptance-server-f67i2kr0/budgets-workspace-restore-a-uds/run-r1 — the very directory the killed daemon's run r1 was using. `materialize_workspaces` copies the base image onto that path with `std::fs::copy`, which truncates the existing copy in place, so the previous instance's retained volume (sha256 05a3e86874eb74e64d7ed822e4d54eb0caf14ee70a38c478b54c6f4c18cf7285) is replaced (sha256 a6d7281595cd60234f1f2f028790f6f23a4e7264309037c4a28ac395f89b6031) and its /workspace/notes.txt marker is gone. The block slice's contract that a run's copies stay after the run (they hold the agent's work) therefore holds only within one daemon lifetime: restarting on the same --uds-dir destroys the retained volumes of the runs whose ids the new daemon re-issues. Both behaviours are deliberate on their own (run ids are per-daemon; copies are kept), which is the conflict this cell records.
findings.expected: the retained copy of a finished/killed run keeps its bytes across a daemon restart (or the new run is given a path that cannot collide with one)
findings.reproducer: noded --workspace IMG --uds-dir D; POST {n:1,beats:40}; console `wspace TOKEN`; `sync`; SIGTERM noded; noded --workspace IMG --uds-dir D; POST {n:1} -> the new run is r1 and D/run-r1/workspace-0.ext4 no longer contains TOKEN
findings.suspected_component: crates/noded/src/registry.rs (reserve_run_id / boot_run run-dir path) + crates/vmm/src/spawner.rs (materialize_workspaces copies in place)
